cards.intuition: BM25 misses meaning when no terms are shared; embeddings blur the exact strings that carry identity. Each has a blind spot the other covers.
cards.formula: sparse fails on paraphrase, dense fails on identifiers
cards.topic: Why Sparse and Dense Retrieval Fail Differently

cards.intuition: Because the two systems miss largely different documents, merging their lists covers more than either alone, often far more than naive averaging suggests.
cards.formula: union recall > max(single recall) when errors are uncorrelated
cards.topic: Why Sparse and Dense Retrieval Fail Differently

cards.intuition: Classify traffic before choosing machinery: exact and navigational queries favor sparse, conceptual and paraphrased queries favor dense.
cards.formula: segment queries -> check which system fails where
cards.topic: Why Sparse and Dense Retrieval Fail Differently

cards.intuition: Merge rankings by giving each document a small payment for every list it appears in, with higher ranks paying slightly more. No scores involved.
cards.formula: RRF(d) = sum over lists of 1/(k + rank), k = 60

cards.intuition: A document ranked 2nd in both lists beats one ranked 1st in a single list: agreement across independent systems is stronger evidence than one system's enthusiasm.
Small k makes top ranks dominate; large k flattens toward a pure vote. 60 is the battle-tested default and tuning it rarely pays.
cards.formula: k up -> flatter, k down -> sharper

cards.intuition: Min-max normalization is hostage to one outlier score, and z-score assumes a symmetry BM25's heavy tail does not have.
cards.formula: outlier max -> all other scores compressed

cards.intuition: Rescale, saturate, or swap the model: any monotone change to scores leaves ranks, and therefore RRF, untouched.
Embedding upgrades shift score distributions, so fitted normalizations silently rot. Ranks never drift, which matters more than the last metric point.
Both retrievers run in parallel, RRF merges them, filters clean the list, and the cross-encoder rescores the survivors.
cards.topic: The Atrium Pattern: BM25 + Vectors + RRF + Reranker

cards.intuition: Vectors down means BM25-only fusion; reranker down means the fused order. Each degraded mode is evaluated offline, never improvised.
cards.formula: every fallback is a tested configuration
cards.topic: The Atrium Pattern: BM25 + Vectors + RRF + Reranker

cards.intuition: Four honest knobs: per-source depth, RRF k, rerank depth, chunk size. Each maps to exactly one metric, so change one at a time.
cards.formula: source depth, k, rerank depth, chunk size
cards.topic: The Atrium Pattern: BM25 + Vectors + RRF + Reranker
